title: Release Chorography Runbook and Traffic Ramp Simulations
content:
Purpose: quick working runbook for the Nov 2026 experimental rollout. This doc collects the preflight checklist, a compact 7-day rollout calendar, traffic ramp experiments we will run in the staging->prod handoff window, and a short decision log of unresolved choices.

High-level objective:
- Ship the platform routing changes that enable model-variant fallback and per-tenant throttles with minimal user-visible disruption. Target SLA: 99.95% p95 latency within 20% of baseline.
- Validate traffic scaling heuristics across dedicated pools and hosted fallback in a silent ramp. Verify cost signal doesn't cause premature fallback.

Audience: release operators, on-call SREs, serving-runtime engineers, partner account leads. This is a working doc; use links to tickets for canonical artifacts.

Preflight checklist (must be green before any traffic shift):
1) Code & infra
   - All PRs merged and CI green: RE-4122, RE-4125.
   - Infra change set applied to staging cluster (tag: release-choro-2026-11).
   - Canary images baked & signed: registry/redwood/choro:2026-11-09.
2) Observability
   - Synthetic smoke tests passing in staging for core endpoints (text.generate, chat.stream, embeddings.batch).
   - Telemetry dashboards deployed: "Chorography Release Pulse" and "KV Cache Hit Rate".
   - Alert burn-in period defined (48h) with suppression for noisy new metrics.
3) Safety gates & feature flags
   - Canary flag toggles validated (FF:choro-fallback-local, FF:choro-prefetch).
   - Rollback playbook staged with exact commands and expected time-to-recover.
4) Capacity & cost
   - Dedicated pool headroom >= 30% at expected peak.
   - Cost guardrails: if cost/unit increases > 18% for 60m, auto step-down to quantized variant.
5) Communication
   - Slack channel #release-chorography created and subscribed by SRE, serving, product.
   - Customer-impact list reviewed; three enterprise customers on white-glove notified.

7-day rollout calendar (compact):
- Day -4 (Nov 10): Finalize runbook; ops rehearsal at 10:00 PT.
- Day -3 (Nov 11): Deploy to canary subset (1% traffic). Monitor 2x p95 and custom quality evals.
- Day -2 (Nov 12): Increase to 5% if canary-green. Run 'variant-resilience' synthetic queries.
- Day -1 (Nov 13): Shadow routing enabled for 100% production traffic (no user-visible switch). Collect divergence metrics.
- Day 0 (Nov 14): Gradual traffic ramp: 10% -> 30% -> 60% over 8h windows with checkpoints.
- Day +1 (Nov 15): Stable at target; run post-rollout smoke and QoR evals.
- Day +3 (Nov 17): Decision window close; finalize notes and toggle auto-fallback policies permanently.

Traffic ramp experiments and hypotheses:
- Experiment A: burst-protect vs steady-ramp
  Hypothesis: small frequent bursts (10% increments every 30m) increase tail latency more than fewer larger steps. We will run A on Day 0 early window for 2h and compare p95 and timeout rates.
- Experiment B: KV prefetch aggressiveness
  Hypothesis: prefetching top-3 prefixes reduces cold-start token cost but slightly increases memory pressure. Metric trade-off: tokens/sec cost vs gmem-utilization. Run B in canary at 5% for 24h.
- Experiment C: cost-threshold auto-stepdown
  Hypothesis: a 15% cost bump sustained for 45m indicates model mismatch; auto-stepdown prevents larger regressions. Validate by intentionally toggling heavier payloads in staging.

Rollback scenarios (fastest to slowest):
- Fast abort (minutes): Disable feature flag chorofallback via FF service -> traffic instantly reverts to baseline routing. Verify rollback by running a smoke batch and confirming token-per-request distribution.
- Regional failover (30-60m): Shift affected region traffic to fallback region and enable dedicated-standby pool. Requires coordinated DNS update + traffic router change.
- Full rollback (1-2h): Revert deployment to previous image tag and rehydrate caches from pre-snapshot. Expected throughput dip for ~30m while caches warm.

Smoke test suite (commands & quick checks):
- curl -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/text.generate -d @smoke-query.json -> expect 200 + latency < 600ms for small prompts.
- run: ./scripts/telemetry/check_heatmap.sh --window=10m --dashboard=choro-pulse -> alert if p95 > baseline*1.3
- sampling query set: /tools/release/evals/choro/small-sample-50.json

Decision log (open decisions flagged early):
- D1: TTL for fallback cache invalidation. Options: 30m / 2h / 6h. Preference: 2h for cost/quality balance. Action: Priya to validate with simulation by Nov 12.
- D2: Quantization profile for model-variant. Choices: q4_0 (fast) vs q8_0 (higher fidelity). Action: Ava to run 48h eval of output divergence against golden set.
- D3: Canary ramp cadence. Proposed: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%. Alternative: 1%, 5%, 30%, 100%. Action: defer to on-call SRE on Day -3 based on canary noise.

Notes to self / loose ends:
- Add example rollback commands to ops-runbook snippet (copy from /playbooks/rollback-examples).
- Confirm if legal flagged any customer contracts for this routing change (contact legal@redwood).
- Need to coordinate with Dedicated sales to avoid trying rollout during scheduled customer migration on Nov 16.

Post-release checklist (what to capture in the release notes):
- Summary of change & rationale.
- Timeline of rollout steps and timestamps for each ramp.
- Key metrics observed (p95 latency, error rate, token cost delta).
- Any incidents and corrective actions.
- Final decision on open D1-D3 and why.

Appendix: quick links and commands:
- staging dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/choro-release-pulse
- canary toggle: https://ff.redwood.company/flags/choro-fallback-local
- rollback script: git+ssh://git@github.com/redwood/release-scripts.git#scripts/fast-rollback.sh

If anything is unclear or you find a gap in the simulations, add a note with tag [ACTION] and assign in the Jira ticket RE-4122.

End of runbook (working draft).
